solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greeting small child going round southeastern US park (8)

indicators.note: the greeting and the child together travel round the SE, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a little one on a trip round the American Southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the park in the southeast, but Yosemite is in California; "southeastern" is only there for its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Yosemite is one of the best-known US national parks, in California's Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Bridge player in a couple of years will be insubstantial (6)

indicators.note: the bridge player goes inside the pair of years

blocks.note: the four bridge players are North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A card player predicts that within two years their game will amount to nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeasty in the sense of frothy is an older meaning: light, all foam and no body, like the head on beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty can mean frothy and trivial, lacking substance.

clue.text: Brother wrapped in considerable melancholy (6)

indicators.note: BR is enclosed by the word for considerable

explanation.surface: A monk is sunk in deep gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: "Considerable melancholy" reads as a single phrase, but "considerable" is wordplay and "melancholy" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sombre mood is a dark, gloomy one.

clue.text: Millions, say, back US spreading its wealth (9)

indicators.note: the letters of BACK US are spread out and rearranged

blocks.note: eg = for example, which 'say' also means

explanation.surface: A plea for the United States to share its riches around, backed by millions.
explanation.walkthrough: "Back US" reads as support for America, but it is six letters to be scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Megabucks is slang for a huge amount of money.

clue.text: Setter scared to broadcast ways to create crosswords? (5,7)

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is nervous about going on air to explain how puzzles are made.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter really would be scared to reveal how clues are built, which is why the question mark covers the definition: a setter's methods are the tricks of the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade secrets are a craft's private methods, here a setter's ways of building clues.

clue.text: Attempt sales pitch but not one offering truthful words (6)

indicators.note: one is I, so the I is taken out

explanation.surface: A salesman tries his pitch, though none of it is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: "But not one" sounds like part of the salesman story; in crosswords one is often I, and here it is the I that comes out of SPIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel, or gospel truth, is something to be taken as wholly true.

clue.text: Open deliveries on time (5)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries (balls bowled)

explanation.surface: A parcel company promises to open its deliveries punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: "Deliveries" suggests parcels, but it is the cricket sense: a bowler delivers six balls in an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open, done in plain view.

clue.text: Knowledgeable person with way to retain big sporting event, though cut by 50 per cent (8)

indicators.note: the way holds the sporting event inside it
only half the event's name is kept

blocks.note: the first four of the eight letters

explanation.surface: An expert travels a route to a major sports event, though with half the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cut by 50 per cent" reads like a budget cut; it halves the eight-letter event name to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is someone learned in many subjects.

clue.text: Well-read intelligent bloke finally replacing book in collection of books (8)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the two words
those letters take the place of the book's B

blocks.note: a library is a collection of books
b = book, the letter that comes out
last letters of intelligenT and blokE

explanation.surface: A clever, bookish man is the last to put a book back on the library shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: "Intelligent bloke" looks like a description of the well-read man, but both words are only there for their last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes someone well-read and fond of books.

clue.text: Drink supplier losing first account to stock good brandy (8)

indicators.note: something that loses its first has shed its opening letter, so the B drops off
a shop stocks goods by keeping them inside, so ARMAN keeps G inside it

blocks.note: ac = account, as on a bank statement

explanation.surface: A bar supplier, down on their first account, stocks a fine brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Good brandy" looks like one phrase, but "good" only gives G; "account to stock good" also hides that ARMAN, not AC, holds the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Armagnac is a particular brandy, distilled in Gascony in southwest France.

clue.text: Grape variety in sheer endless quantity (6)

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: MERE (sheer, as in 'sheer luck') without its last letter

explanation.surface: A grape grown in vast, seemingly unlimited amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sheer" looks like it describes the quantity, but it is its own word, MERE, as in 'sheer chance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Merlot is one of the most widely planted red wine grapes.

clue.text: Get policeman active in attractive location? (8,4)

indicators.note: the letters are set moving

explanation.surface: A call to put a police officer to work somewhere pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: "Attractive" reads as scenic, but the question mark flags magnetism: the magnetic pole is where a compass is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic pole is the point that magnetically attracts.

clue.text: Temperature right in part of cooker to produce strong vibration (5)

indicators.note: R goes inside the part of the cooker

blocks.note: the hob is the top of a cooker, where the pans sit

explanation.surface: Setting the right temperature on the cooker makes it hum.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is the flat top of a cooker, where the pans sit; "right" goes inside it and "Temperature" stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a throb is a strong pulse, like a heartbeat or a bass note.

clue.text: Metal ores transformed into rubbery material (9)

indicators.note: the letters change their form

explanation.surface: An alchemist's boast: metal ores turned into rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is alchemy, turning metal into something else, and that is exactly what the anagram does to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is a rubber-like polymer.

clue.text: Hide legal document about rejected studio employee (12)

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so RE is written back to front

blocks.note: a writ is a court order

explanation.surface: A film studio hides a lawsuit against a worker it has let go.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hide" looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to screen something is to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenwriter writes scripts for a film studio.

clue.text: Complex procedure to arrange graduate function (9)

explanation.surface: Organising a graduation party turns out to be a long palaver.
explanation.walkthrough: "Graduate function" reads as a graduation party, but the two words are split: the graduate is an MA and the function is a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rigmarole is a tediously involved business, like the paperwork for a visa.

clue.text: Civil agency worker having exam (8)

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker from an agency
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A civil service temp sits a test.
explanation.walkthrough: "Civil" reads as polite; here it means secular, as opposed to religious, which is what temporal means in 'the lords spiritual and temporal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means secular or civil, as opposed to church matters.

clue.text: I initially recognise British novelist in trade union? That’s sweet (8)

indicators.note: take the first letter of recognise
everything before goes inside the trade union

blocks.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

explanation.surface: Someone spots a famous writer at a union meeting and finds it a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: "I initially recognise" reads as one phrase, but "initially" works only on "recognise"; the I stays whole. "British novelist" is Amis, Kingsley or Martin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert; a sweet is a pudding in British use.

clue.text: Withdrawal scheme? Continue to accept half of it and assess limits to generosity (4,8)

indicators.note: the verb takes the half of IT inside it
IT has two letters, so half of it is a single letter, here the T
the first and last letters of generosity

blocks.note: to exist = to go on, continue

explanation.surface: A plan to back out: keep going, accept half, and judge how generous to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark on "Withdrawal scheme" warns that it is loose: an exit strategy is a plan for getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit strategy is a planned way of withdrawing from a situation.

clue.text: Cocktail — there’s a certain charm about it (6)

indicators.note: about means around, so the charm sits all round IT

blocks.note: mojo = a magic charm, or personal magnetism

explanation.surface: A cocktail with a certain charm to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a drinks-menu description, which hides that "it" is simply two letters to be wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mojito is a rum cocktail with mint and lime.

clue.text: Surreptitious cuddling remains vulgar (6)

indicators.note: the word for surreptitious wraps its arms round the remains

blocks.note: ashes are what remain after burning

explanation.surface: A secret embrace strikes someone as crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly is old slang for sly or knowing, which is how it stands in for "surreptitious". "Remains" looks like a verb but it is the noun, as in ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something flashy is showy in a tasteless way, which is one sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Fix one’s habitual response about area of instrumental technique (9)

indicators.note: the letters before it go round A

blocks.note: a tic is a habitual twitch

explanation.surface: Someone wants to cure their nervous habit in one part of their playing.
explanation.walkthrough: "About" sits late in the clue, so it tells everything before it to go round the area; the A ends up as the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianistic means relating to piano technique.

clue.text: Digital assistant upset with hard language (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: SIRI, Apple's voice assistant, turned round

explanation.surface: A voice assistant takes offence at some rough language.
explanation.walkthrough: "Upset" and "hard language" suggest swearing at a phone, but the language is a national one.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Irish, or Irish Gaelic, is one language among many.

clue.text: Twelve letters left in key (5)

blocks.note: A to L covers twelve letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle with twelve letters left over in the answer key.
explanation.walkthrough: "Twelve letters" is read as a span of the alphabet: A to L. The key is a low coral island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a low island, and an atoll is a ring-shaped coral island.

clue.text: Dried fruit is kept in bucket? (6)

indicators.note: IS is held inside the word for bucket

blocks.note: to bucket (down) is to rain heavily

explanation.surface: Dried fruit stored in a pail.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bucket" looks like a noun, but the question mark flags the verb: when it's bucketing down, it is pouring with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a raisin is one kind of dried fruit, made from grapes.

clue.text: Source welcoming British science backing AI-related science? (8)

indicators.note: the source takes B inside it
backing means moving backwards, so SCI is read from the end

blocks.note: the root is the source of something

explanation.surface: A source says Britain is embracing science that supports artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a loose definition: robotics often uses AI but is engineering rather than AI itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics is the science of robots, which are closely tied to artificial intelligence.

clue.text: Sinister expression of discomfort in French article (6)

indicators.note: the cry goes inside the article

explanation.surface: A menacing look of unease appears in a French newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: "French article" is not a newspaper piece; it is a grammatical article, LE, meaning 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means shady or disreputable, with a sinister air.

clue.text: German thinker dismissing pound currency having dismissed English dominance (8)

indicators.note: the thinker sends away his L
the currency has sent away its E

blocks.note: HEGEL without L (pound, from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A German philosopher spurns sterling and cash stripped of Englishness in pursuit of dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound is L from the Latin libra, as in £. The two deletions mirror each other: the thinker drops a letter, then the currency does.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegemony is dominance, especially of one state over others.
